newsitem.title: CHILE: Foreign buying pushes Chilean shrs to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying pushes Chilean shrs to record highs.

text.p: Chilean stormed to record highs on heavy buying by foreign institutional investors, mainly in the electricity and telecommunications sectors.

Profit taking in the final hour took some luster off the day's gains but the IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares still ended 2.84 percent up at 133.57 points. The all-share IGPA rose 1.47 percent to to 5735.13 points on thumping volume of 33 billion pesos.
"It's all foreign buying, not much locally," said a trader. "Sooner or later there's going to be an adjustment. There are already people waiting to start taking profits."
"The IPSA has already gone up 33 percent this year and people were expecting it to rise 20, 25 percent for the whole year, so I think it's a question of time before we backtrack a bit," he said.
Stagnating stock prices in emerging markets in Eastern Europe and elsewhere are driving yield-hungry U.S. mutual funds to Latin America, especially Chile, brokers said .

The biggest gainers included telecom stocks, largely on reports Telefonica de Espana's Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile (CTC) was near a merger deal with rival VTR, owned by the Luksic group and Southwestern Bell.

In Madrid, a Telefonica spokesman said talks with VTR were in "advanced stages." CTC's A and B series were among the day's biggest gainers, rising 7.7 percent and 8.5 percent to 3,695 pesos and 2,995 pesos, respectively.
Other telecom stocks also rose on the prospect of less competition in the long-distance market, with Telex-Chile up 2.6 percent to 1180 pesos and Entel up 1.8 percent to 3,240 pesos.
Electricity stocks also rose, still reaping the benefits of an end to a year-long drought which hurt hydroelectric dams. Chile depends heavily on hydro power.
"Electricity shares go up everytime it rains now," said a broker.
Endesa rose 2.3 percent to 309 pesos and its holding company Enersis was up 3.4 percent to 290 pesos.

Chilgener, which, as a fossil fuel generator, would not benefit directly from the end to the drought, was also up after holding relatively flat in recent sessions, gaining 4.8 percent to 173 pesos on the day's top stock by volume.
Cervecerias Unidas winery unit Vina San Pedro rose on reports of a capital increase but then fell back and ended unchanged at 3.25 pesos.
The 21 decliners, against 61 gainers, included several stocks in the CB group, including CB Capitales, off 12 percent to 18.5 pesos, and Santander, off 1.6 percent to 29.50 pesos.
